scenarios.title: Unfair Criticism
scenarios.description: Your manager publicly criticizes your project in front of the entire team, calling it "poorly thought out" and "unprofessional." You feel this criticism is unfair and exaggerated, especially given that you followed all the guidelines provided and the project met its initial objectives.

strategies.name: Cognitive Reappraisal
strategies.description: Try to reframe the situation - maybe my manager is under pressure, or this feedback could help me improve future projects

strategies.name: Emotional Suppression
strategies.description: Keep my emotions hidden and act professionally, not letting anyone see how upset I am

strategies.name: Direct Expression
strategies.description: Speak up immediately to defend my work and challenge the unfair criticism

strategies.name: Seeking Support
strategies.description: Talk to trusted colleagues or friends about the situation to process my emotions

scenarios.title: Overwhelming Deadline
scenarios.description: You've just been told that a major project deadline has been moved up by two weeks, meaning you now have to complete in 3 days what you planned to do over the next 2.5 weeks. Your workload is already at capacity, and you're not sure how you'll manage to deliver quality work under this new timeline.

strategies.name: Problem-Focused Coping
strategies.description: Immediately start planning and prioritizing - break down tasks and see what can be streamlined or delegated

strategies.name: Acceptance & Adaptation
strategies.description: Accept that the situation is challenging but focus on doing my best within the constraints

strategies.name: Avoidance
strategies.description: Try not to think about the deadline too much and work on other tasks first

strategies.name: Emotional Venting
strategies.description: Express my frustration to my manager about the unrealistic timeline

scenarios.title: Team Conflict
scenarios.description: During a team meeting, a colleague takes credit for an idea you proposed weeks ago and presents it as their own innovation. When you try to speak up, they interrupt and dismiss your input. Other team members seem to go along with their version of events.

strategies.name: Diplomatic Response
strategies.description: Calmly mention my earlier contribution and suggest we collaborate on developing the idea further

strategies.name: Direct Confrontation
strategies.description: Clearly state that this was my idea and provide evidence of when I first proposed it

strategies.name: Strategic Withdrawal
strategies.description: Let it go for now but document everything and address it privately with my manager later

strategies.name: Emotional Distance
strategies.description: Detach emotionally and view this as a learning experience about office politics

low_reactivity.description: Low emotional reactivity - tends to stay calm under pressure

moderate_reactivity.description: Moderate emotional reactivity - typical stress responses

high_reactivity.description: High emotional reactivity - consider stress management techniques

excellent.description: Strong emotion regulation skills with adaptive strategies and controlled reactivity

good.description: Good emotion regulation with mostly adaptive approaches

moderate.description: Moderate emotion regulation - mix of adaptive and less effective strategies

needs_improvement.description: Consider developing more adaptive emotion regulation strategies

instructions: This assessment evaluates how you manage difficult emotions in workplace situations. For each scenario, rate your initial emotional intensity and select your preferred coping strategy.
